_about: Decision-model benchmark corpus (2026-09-26). Labels were written by the AI assistant (Claude) that built the benchmark, BEFORE any model was run, against the criteria below. They are not human-annotated ground truth: treat agreement as agreement with these written criteria. Interview scores are benchmarked separately on apps/interviews/benchmark_cases.json (50 cases, score bands written in earlier loops, also AI-authored).

criteria.addresses: yes = describes something the candidate did that answers every part of what was asked; partly = on the subject asked about but misses a requested part, or stays general / unclear about their own part; no = a non-answer (declines, does not know) or about a different subject.
criteria.evidence: sufficient = at least one specific action of their own AND at least one concrete detail (tool, figure, named artefact or outcome) that bears on the question; otherwise insufficient.
criteria.followup: yes = the answer is on the subject but leaves a gap worth one probing question (missing outcome or method, an unexplained claim, a contradiction, an unclear own role); no = the answer is complete, or it is a non-answer / off-topic, where the interview moves on.
criteria.requirement: satisfied = the CV shows the candidate using the skill in described work (named or unmistakably described); partial = the skill is only listed or mentioned, with no described use, or only coursework; missing = neither named nor described (a similarly named different skill does not count).

relevance.question: Tell me about a time you added an index in PostgreSQL to fix a slow query. What did you check before and after?
relevance.answer: Our bookings report took about 40 seconds. I ran EXPLAIN ANALYZE, saw a sequential scan on hotel_id and check_in, added a composite index on those two columns, built it CONCURRENTLY, and ran EXPLAIN ANALYZE again: an index scan, and the report came back in under a second.

relevance.question: Describe a usability test you ran on a prototype. What did you change because of it?
relevance.answer: I tested a Figma prototype of our checkout with six hotel guests. Four of them missed the promo-code field, so I moved it above the total and tested again; all six found it the second time.

relevance.question: Tell me about a patient whose condition changed during your shift. What did you do?
relevance.answer: A post-op patient's oxygen saturation fell to 88% at 3 a.m. I sat him up, started 2 litres of oxygen per the standing order, called the on-call doctor with his observations, and rechecked every 15 minutes; he was back at 95% within the hour.

relevance.answer: I think technology changes very quickly these days and everyone has to keep learning. When I was at university we had many group projects and I learned that communication is really important, and that you should always respect your teammates and listen to their ideas. I also think time management is important because deadlines come fast, and I use a calendar app to plan my week. In the future I want to become a senior engineer and maybe lead a team one day.

relevance.question: Describe a time you improved the conversion rate of a landing page.
relevance.answer: Marketing is a very creative field and I have always loved creativity. Since I was young I enjoyed drawing and later photography, and I have a big Instagram following for my travel pictures from Mustang and Rara. I believe that brands should tell stories and connect emotionally with people, and that is what I would bring to your company because I am passionate and hard-working.

relevance.answer: Accounting is the language of business, as my professor used to say, and I agree that numbers tell a story about every company. I have studied IFRS and I think the standards are very well designed, although some parts are complicated. I also follow the stock market in Nepal and I think NEPSE has a lot of potential if more people invest.

relevance.question: Walk me through a time you made a slow test suite faster. What did you change?
relevance.answer: At Phewa Stays the booking API was on Flask and p95 was about 900 ms. I profiled it with Django Debug Toolbar after moving it to Django REST Framework, found N+1 queries in the room serializer, added select_related and prefetch_related, and p95 dropped to 250 ms.

relevance.question: Tell me about a time you added an index in PostgreSQL to fix a slow query.
relevance.answer: A guest complained she was charged twice for one night. I apologised, checked the payment records with our accountant, found the duplicate charge and refunded it the same afternoon. She left a five-star review and booked again the next month.

relevance.question: Describe how you ran usability research with real users.
relevance.answer: I rebuilt our whole design system in Figma: 120 components down to 45, with tokens for colour and spacing, and engineering adoption went from two squads to all six in a quarter. It was the biggest project of my career.

relevance.question: Tell me about a schema change you ran on a live database. How did you make it safe, and how would you have rolled it back?
relevance.answer: We needed a new nullable column on bookings. I added it with no default so the table was not rewritten, and backfilled it in batches of 10,000 rows overnight.

relevance.question: Describe a campaign you ran. How did you measure it, and what did it return?
relevance.answer: I ran a Facebook campaign for off-season bookings with a discount code and a landing page, targeting families in Kathmandu over three weeks.

relevance.question: Tell me about a time you onboarded a new team member. What did you do, and how did you know it worked?
relevance.answer: I wrote a one-page checklist for the first week, paired with her on her first three pull requests and booked a daily 15-minute check-in.

relevance.question: Tell me about a time you made an API endpoint safe to retry.
relevance.answer: Added an idempotency key to POST /payments, stored with a unique constraint; repeats returned the stored result. Double charges stopped.

relevance.question: Describe a time you reduced a report's run time.
relevance.answer: Replaced a per-row query loop with one GROUP BY in SQL; the monthly report went from 12 minutes to 20 seconds.

relevance.question: Tell me about a time you resolved a stock discrepancy in a warehouse.
relevance.answer: Counted the bay twice, traced 40 missing cartons to a mis-scanned transfer, corrected the transfer and retrained the scanner shift.

relevance.question: Tell me about a production incident you led. What was the cause and what did you change?
relevance.answer: Incidents are always stressful and it is important to stay calm. In my experience the most important thing is communication with the team and stakeholders, and making sure everyone knows what is happening. We always did a proper post-mortem after incidents and tried to learn from them. I believe a blameless culture is very important, and that monitoring and alerting should be set up properly so problems are found early. I always try to be proactive.

relevance.question: Describe a design you changed after user feedback. What exactly did you change?
relevance.answer: User feedback is the heart of good design and I always take it very seriously. I believe in iterating quickly and listening to users, and I have used many tools like surveys, interviews and analytics over the years. Feedback helped me improve my designs many times, and I think every designer should be humble and open to criticism.

relevance.question: Tell me about a budget you managed. How did you keep it on track?
relevance.answer: Budgets are very important for any organisation and I always make sure to be careful with money. I think planning is key, as well as regular reviews and good communication with the finance team. I have been responsible for budgets in several roles and always tried to be transparent and accountable.

relevance.question: Tell me about a time you improved a delivery process.
relevance.answer: Our riders left the depot in the order parcels were loaded. I grouped the 60 daily parcels by ward on a Google Sheet the night before and printed a route per rider; average delivery time fell from 3.5 hours to 2 hours over a month.

relevance.question: Describe a lesson you taught that did not work the first time. What did you change?
relevance.answer: My first lesson on Ohm's law for Grade 11 lost half the class; only 12 of 30 passed the exit quiz. I rebuilt it around a circuit kit each group assembled and measured, and 26 of 30 passed the same quiz the next week.

relevance.question: Tell me about a time you found a security problem in your own code.
relevance.answer: In code review of my own login endpoint I noticed I compared tokens with ==, which leaks timing. I switched to hmac.compare_digest, added a rate limit of 5 attempts a minute, and wrote a test for both.

relevance.question: Tell me about an API you made faster. How did you find the cause, and what did you change?
relevance.answer: I reduced the latency of our main API by 90% and it became the fastest service in the company. Everyone was very happy with the result.

relevance.question: Describe a campaign you ran and how you measured it.
relevance.answer: My campaign tripled our sales and was the most successful in the company's history. The numbers were amazing.

relevance.question: Tell me about a team you led through a difficult project.
relevance.answer: I led the best team in the company and we delivered everything perfectly and ahead of schedule. I am a natural leader.

relevance.question: Tell me about a time you reduced errors in a process.
relevance.answer: I brought the error rate on invoices down to zero with a new checklist. After that we still had about 15 wrong invoices a month, mostly the same kind as before.

relevance.question: Describe a deployment you ran with no downtime.
relevance.answer: I deployed the new booking service with zero downtime using blue-green deployment. The site was down for about 40 minutes while we switched the database over.

relevance.question: Tell me about a time you finished a project early.
relevance.answer: We delivered the mobile app two weeks early. The launch was delayed by a month because testing was not finished, but it was early.

relevance.question: Tell me about a time you handled a data breach or security incident.
relevance.answer: We had something like that once and it was handled. Things were fine after that and we moved on.

relevance.question: Describe a time you disagreed with your manager about a design.

relevance.question: Tell me about a time you trained a colleague.
relevance.answer: We did some training with the new people around then, it was part of how things worked in the team.

relevance.question: Tell me about a time you designed an onboarding flow. What changed for users?
relevance.answer: I redesigned our hotel-owner onboarding in Figma from nine screens to four, cut the optional fields and added progress dots, then handed it to engineering.

relevance.question: Tell me about a time you automated a manual task. What was the result?
relevance.answer: I wrote a Python script with pandas that pulls the daily bank export, matches it against our booking ledger and emails the finance team a list of unmatched rows.

relevance.question: Describe a negotiation you handled with a supplier. What did you get?
relevance.answer: Our linen supplier raised prices twice in a year. I gathered quotes from three other suppliers and met the owner with them to renegotiate our contract.
